title: Linearized headroom dampening for microbatch control at extreme QPS
creator: Asha Patel
description: When traffic spikes above sustained QPS targets, our continuous batching control sometimes oscillates: aggressive admission causes headroom exhaustion and KV cache thrashing, then the system over-corrects and under-utilizes GPUs. This ticket implements a linearized headroom dampening controller that smooths microbatch admission by combining short-term occupancy estimates, KV cache pressure signals, and a lightweight slot-occupancy predictor. The goal is to reduce queues, avoid KV evictions, and keep p95 tail latency within SLO without large throughput loss.
acceptance_criteria: p95 generation latency remains <= 1200ms under 3x baseline QPS synthetic workload
KV cache eviction rate reduced by >= 35% on high QPS bursts compared to current controller
GPU memory OOMs eliminated in replayed customer incidents (replays attached)
No more than 7% sustained throughput loss at 99th percentile of traffic spikes
Feature gated and rollouts reversible via console with metrics dashboard
design_notes: Introduce a linearized headroom signal H_t computed every 20ms: H_t = G - (alpha * estimated_slots_used + beta * kv_eviction_pressure + gamma * recent_batch_growth)
Admission probability p_admit = sigmoid(k * H_t + b) with configurable slope k and bias b to avoid binary thresholds
Slot predictor: exponential moving average of slot occupancy with per-model decay factor to respect varying seq lengths
KV pressure signal derived from two counters: eviction_rate_per_minute and kv_read_latency_95. Normalize into 0..1 scale via historical baselining

Memory safety: conservative headroom floor tied to per-GPU reserved slab (configurable by deployment). If H_t < floor, immediately switch to emergency shedding mode with prioritized routing to fallback models
All controller parameters exposed as JSON config in runtime flags and as console knobs for dedicated customers
experiment_plan: Phase 0: Unit tests and sims using synthetic token length distributions (short/long/mixed) to validate non-oscillatory behavior
Phase 1: Canary on 1% of traffic for a single CFD cluster with low critical workloads; monitor KV evictions, latency, and throughput for 48h
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 10% then 30% across clusters with different models and sequence length profiles; enable automatic rollback on violation of any acceptance criteria
Collect detailed traces (prefix age, batch size distribution, KV hit/miss, GPU memory free) and push to temporary observability board
rollout_plan: Deploy runtime change behind flag to all regions (no traffic changes yet)
Enable flag for canary cluster; 48h measure -> stakeholder review
If stable, ramp to 30% over 72h and run long-tail stability tests for additional 7 days
If regressions seen, immediately flip flag off and gather postmortem data
metrics: Average and max microbatch size distribution
Rollout rollback triggers: latency breach, eviction spike, OOM events
risks: Under-dampening may still allow oscillations leading to intermittent KV thrashing
Over-dampening can reduce effective throughput and increase cost per token
Model-specific sequence length variance may require per-model tuning parameters
Console knobs introduce operational complexity for customers on Dedicated/private deployments
qa_steps: Run replay of three customer incidents (links below) with controller off and on, compare metrics
Inject synthetic spike traffic using loadgen with randomized seq lengths and confirm acceptance criteria
Fault injection: simulate delayed KV responses and ensure controller degrades gracefully
Memory safety test: force memory pressure in lab cluster to verify emergency shedding triggers
notes: Initial simulator results show a 42% reduction in eviction spikes with only a 3% throughput drop under synthetic 4x QPS bursts
We should coordinate with Console team to add a single toggle and a pre-baked dashboard for canaries
Follow-up ticket planned to evaluate per-model auto-calibration of alpha/beta/gamma coefficients
